title: KV cache precision scheduling and calibration playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: define and execute a reproducible playbook for calibrating INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles for the KV cache, measure latency/quality trade-offs, and prototype a lightweight precision-scheduling controller for production rollouts. This ticket captures experiment design, data/metric requirements, automation steps for calibration sweeps, and rollout/rollback criteria.

Background: prior experiments focused on static per-model quant profiles and offline accuracy checks. KV cache quantization introduces unique failure modes: small errors in key/value tensors can amplify across long prefixes, and runtime cache layout/alignment alters quantization sensitivity. We need a systematic calibration pipeline that: 1) generates per-layer calibration stats for attention K/V, 2) sweeps INT8/FP8/stochastic rounding variants, 3) evaluates both model quality and request-level latency/SLA impact, and 4) produces safe rollout artifacts (profiles + gating rules) for the serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline produces repeatable per-layer scaling factors and a canonical artifact (profile) for each model and precision variant.
Benchmarks show at least one INT8 or FP8 profile with <=0.6% relative QA EM regression (or equivalent metric) and p95 latency < runtime-1.20 SLA target for medium batch workloads.
A precision-scheduling prototype can switch KV precision at route-level with graceful fallback to FP16 within 500ms of detecting quality drift.
Automation produces an artifacts bundle (profile, metrics CSV, baseline diffs, rollout gating policy) suitable for review and canary deployment.
Documentation (playbook) outlines minimum dataset, calibration hyperparameters, and rollback criteria for on-call engineers.
experiment_matrix: Models: small/medium/large open models used in catalog (e.g., redwood-v1-small, community-34B). Precisions: FP16 baseline, FP8 e4m3/e5m2 variants, symmetric INT8 with per-channel and per-tensor scales, and hybrid per-layer configs. Batch sizes: [1,4,16], Seq lengths: [64,256,1024] (to capture KV growth). Kernels: default runtime kernels and experimental int8-optimized kernels. Calib datasets: 10k representative prefix+continuation pairs across generation/QA/assistant domains. Metrics: end-to-end latency (p50,p95,p99), inference throughput, tokens/sec cost, QA EM/F1, logit-KL to baseline, embedding cosine similarity, and per-token conditional probability delta. Sweep axis includes stochastic rounding on/off and clip thresholds. Each experiment run must produce reproducible seeds and a metadata file with commit/weights/version.
calibration_workflow: 1) Data selection: sample 10k prefixes stratified by length and domain; hold out 1k for validation. 2) Per-layer statistic collection: run FP16 forward to collect min/max, histograms, and second-order moments for attention K and V tensors separately. 3) Candidate scale generation: derive linear scales for static symmetric/asymmetric int8 and FP8 mantissa/exponent bias candidates. 4) Localized micro-eval: apply candidate scales layerwise (single-layer perturbation) to find high-sensitivity layers. 5) Full-profile sweep: evaluate top-k profile combinations using beam search over layer priorities to limit combinatorial explosion. 6) Quant-deploy harness: run end-to-end generation to capture latency and quality metrics. 7) Profile scoring: compute weighted score combining quality loss and latency delta; rank profiles for trade-off frontier. 8) Artifact packaging: attach profile JSON, calibration stats, metric CSV, and deterministic seed. 9) Rollout gating: define canary percentage schedule, automatic rollback threshold (e.g., quality delta > 1% or p95 latency increase > 10%).
evaluation_plan: Quality metrics: QA EM/F1 on held-out questions, next-token perplexity, logit-KL to FP16 baseline (per-position, aggregated), and embedding cosine similarity for downstream retrieval tasks. Operational metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, observed batching efficiency, tokens/sec, GPU memory footprint delta. Cost proxy: estimated token execution cost normalized to baseline. Statistical tests: bootstrap confidence intervals for quality metrics; require non-overlapping CI for any claimed improvement. Drift detection: run small synthetic continuous test that evaluates recent production prefixes against baseline and new profile using KL divergence and alert if drift exceeds configured threshold. All evaluation runs must be reproducible and tagged with runtime image and kernel versions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Long-prefix amplification where tiny KV quant errors accumulate and produce large quality regressions. Mitigation: prioritize per-layer micro-eval and include long prefix examples in calibration set; enforce conservative clip thresholds for high-sensitivity layers.

Risk: Latency regressions due to misaligned kernels or additional dequant steps. Mitigation: measure p95/p99 across hardware profiles and only enable profiles that pass latency SLAs; add fallbacks to FP16 for heavy tails.

Risk: Non-repeatable calibration due to nondeterministic ops (stochastic rounding). Mitigation: record RNG seeds and run deterministic mode for final profile generation; treat stochastic rounding as an optional experimental flag.

Risk: Hidden distribution shift between calibration data and production traffic. Mitigation: require weekly re-eval on sampled production prefixes and automated gating to rollback if quality drops beyond thresholds.
